lessons.title: Introduction to Databases and SQL

content.title: What is a Database?
content.text: A database is an organized collection of information that can be stored, managed and retrieved efficiently.

content.title: Relational Databases
content.text: A relational database stores information in tables made up of rows and columns. Tables can be related to one another using keys.

content.title: What is SQL?
content.text: SQL stands for Structured Query Language. It is used to communicate with relational database systems and perform operations such as retrieving and modifying data.

content.title: Example Table
content.code:
students
----------------
id | name | age
1  | Anu  | 21
2  | Ravi | 22

key_points: Rows represent records and columns represent attributes.
SQL is used to work with relational databases.

content.title: SELECT
content.text: The SELECT statement is used to retrieve data from a database table.

content.title: DISTINCT
content.text: DISTINCT removes duplicate values from the selected result.

lessons.title: Filtering and Sorting Data

content.title: WHERE
content.text: The WHERE clause filters rows according to a condition.

content.title: Multiple Conditions
ORDER BY
content.text: ORDER BY sorts query results. ASC specifies ascending order and DESC specifies descending order.

content.title: Sorting

key_points: AND requires multiple conditions to be true.
OR allows either condition to be true.

lessons.title: Aggregate Functions and GROUP BY

content.title: Aggregate Functions
content.text: Aggregate functions perform calculations over multiple rows.

content.title: GROUP BY
content.text: GROUP BY divides rows into groups so that aggregate calculations can be performed separately for each group.

content.title: Grouping

key_points: MIN and MAX find minimum and maximum values.
GROUP BY creates groups for aggregation.

lessons.title: SQL Joins

content.title: Why Joins?
content.text: Database information is often divided across multiple tables. Joins allow related records from different tables to be combined.

content.title: Primary and Foreign Keys
content.text: A primary key uniquely identifies a row in a table. A foreign key references a key in another table and can establish a relationship between tables.

content.title: INNER JOIN
content.code:
SELECT students.name, departments.name
FROM students
INNER JOIN departments
ON students.department_id = departments.id;

content.title: INNER JOIN
content.text: INNER JOIN returns rows where the join condition matches in both tables.

content.title: LEFT JOIN
content.text: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table. Missing matches produce NULL values for the right-side columns.

content.title: LEFT JOIN
content.code:
SELECT students.name, departments.name
FROM students
LEFT JOIN departments
ON students.department_id = departments.id;

key_points: LEFT JOIN keeps all records from the left table.

lessons.title: Subqueries and HAVING

content.title: Subqueries
content.text: A subquery is a query nested inside another SQL query. It can be used to calculate or retrieve information needed by the outer query.

content.title: Subquery Example
HAVING
content.text: HAVING filters grouped results after GROUP BY has been applied.

content.title: HAVING Example
content.code:
SELECT department, COUNT(*)
FROM employees
GROUP BY department
HAVING COUNT(*) > 5;

key_points: Subqueries are queries inside other queries.
HAVING is commonly used with GROUP BY.

lessons.title: INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE

content.title: INSERT
content.text: INSERT adds new records to a table.

content.title: UPDATE
content.text: UPDATE modifies existing records. A WHERE condition should normally be used to restrict which records are changed.

content.title: UPDATE Example
DELETE
content.text: DELETE removes records from a table. A missing WHERE condition can remove every record in the table.

key_points: WHERE should be used carefully with UPDATE and DELETE.

content.title: Constraints
content.text: Constraints are rules applied to table data to help maintain accuracy and consistency.

content.title: Table with Constraints
NOT NULL
content.text: NOT NULL prevents a column from containing NULL values.

content.title: UNIQUE
content.text: UNIQUE prevents duplicate values in a constrained column or group of columns.

content.title: Database Integrity
content.text: Good database design uses appropriate keys and constraints to keep stored information consistent.
